situation.summary: Move-out works at 42 Mallowfen Crescent (electric-meter cabinet door hinges, four wall nails and paint in Bedroom 1, sticker residue on the front door) moved to a landlord-managed job. The landlord declined the Pineglass bundle quote of £564.48 on 13 Sept and arranged her own company (E017–E020). On 18 Sept she wrote that the work was completed, with no date, photos, invoice or scope detail (E021). The request was marked completed and its workflow task dismissed (E022, E024). The agency's 08:46 request for an itemised cost breakdown and a tenant-responsibility view has no reply recorded (E023, E025). Completion rests on an unverified email, so the record should not close yet.

decision.actionLabel: Confirm to the landlord that her completion is recorded and ask where the keys are, with this morning's cost and responsibility question restated
decision.message:
Dear Elowen,

Thank you for your email this morning confirming that the move-out works at 42 Mallowfen Crescent have been completed. We have recorded the electric meter cabinet door hinges, the four wall nails and paint touch-up in Bedroom 1, and the sticker residue on the front door as completed by your own company, on your confirmation.

Before we close our records, we need two things from you:

1. Keys: the property is vacant, and keys were to be arranged through our office. Could you let us know where the keys to the property are now, and whether any keys were given to your contractor that still need to come back to us?

2. Costs and responsibility (from my email this morning): if you would like us to review any of these costs against the tenancy account, please send the invoice or an itemised breakdown from the company that did the work, showing the amount and whether VAT is included. Please also tell us which items, if any, you consider to be the former tenant's responsibility. If you are not looking to recover any of these costs, a short reply saying so is enough. Your view does not decide any charge on its own; any proposed charge would be reviewed separately against the check-in and check-out records.

If they are easy to send, photos of the finished work would help support any review, but they are not essential.

Please could you reply by Monday 22 September 2025. We will update you by Tuesday 23 September 2025 on what we have received and what, if anything, is still open.

Kind regards,
Talia Wren
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The landlord stepped in and handled this job herself. She turned down the £564.48 quote and used her own company (E017). We stood Pineglass down (E020), and she has now confirmed the work is done (E021). For a job the landlord manages herself, her confirmation is enough to treat the work as complete, so I am not asking her to prove it. Two things still stop us closing. First, our question from this morning about costs and the former tenant's share has no reply (E023, E025). It was only sent six hours ago, so chasing it now would be too early. Second, the property is empty and keys were being arranged through our office (E003), but nothing records where they are now. We have to check that before closing. The key question has not been asked yet, so it is a new question rather than a chase, and it is worth sending now. Folding this morning's question into the same email keeps it all in one place and adds a reply-by date. This matters because the workflow task was dismissed (E024) and nothing is now prompting a follow-up. The internal note that approval was already given (E001) is contradicted by E012, E015 and E017, so I have ignored it.
decision.expectedOutcome: The landlord says where the keys are and either sends the invoice or breakdown with her view on the tenant's share, or says she is not recovering any costs. That lets us close the job or pass a recharge decision to a person.
boundaries: The landlord's email is her word that the work is done; we have not independently checked the work.
Asking her view on the tenant's share does not establish liability or approve any charge against the former tenant or the deposit.
Nothing here approves, pays or takes on any cost for the work done by the landlord's company.
Sending the email does not mean it has been received or answered.

decision.message: HOLD NOTE (internal), NBL-028, 42 Mallowfen Crescent. Do not close yet, even though the request is marked completed (E022) and the workflow task was dismissed (E024). The landlord is handling the works herself. She declined the Pineglass quote of £564.48 (E017), and Pineglass has been told not to attend (E020). She wrote on 18 Sept that the work is done (E021). That is enough to accept completion on a job she is managing. Two things are still open: 1) Our email of 18 Sept at 08:46 (E023) asked for an itemised breakdown of her costs and whether she thinks any item is the former tenant's responsibility. It has had no reply for about 6 hours, which is too soon to chase. 2) The property is empty and keys were to be arranged through the office (E003), but the records do not show where the keys are now. RECHECK Monday 22 September 2025. If she has not replied, email her (then phone if there is still no answer). Restate the E023 request in full, ask where the keys are and whether they are back with the office, and ask her to reply by Wednesday 24 September 2025. Ask for the date and name of the company that did the work only if she wants the tenancy account reviewed. If she says an item is the former tenant's responsibility, or asks for a deduction, hand the case to a person. That is a recharge/deposit decision; do not decide it here. Close only when the keys are accounted for and she has either answered the cost question or said nothing is to be recharged. Nothing is owed to Pineglass: they were stood down and never attended.
decision.rationale: The landlord chose to arrange the works herself (E017) and has said they are complete (E021). For a job the landlord manages, her word is enough evidence of completion, so we do not need photos or an invoice to close. No contractor is involved and nothing is payable through us. What stops the job being closed is our own open question: at 08:46 today (E023) we asked for her cost breakdown and her view on tenant responsibility. Only about 6 hours have passed (E025). Landlords usually reply within a day or so, and chasing in under about 2 days is premature. On an empty property we also need to know where the keys are before closing. The real risk is that the dismissed workflow task (E024) leaves nothing to prompt a follow-up. A hold with a dated recheck fixes that without sending the landlord a second email on the same day. Monday 22 September is the first working day about 3 days after the ask.
decision.expectedOutcome: The job stays open with a recheck date. By 22 September the landlord has either replied with her costs and responsibility view, which may lead to a hand-over to a person, or she is chased with the full request plus the keys question.

Holding the case does not decide whether the former tenant is responsible for any item or should be charged.
Pineglass's £564.48 quote was declined and is not owed; this hold approves no spend.
The keys' location is not established by anything in the records.

decision.message:
HOLD – NBL-028, 42 Mallowfen Crescent (vacant). The landlord arranged her own company (E017) and on 18 Sept wrote that the work is completed (E021). At 08:46 on 18 Sept we asked her for an itemised cost breakdown and whether she thinks any items are the former tenant's responsibility (E023). There is no reply yet, and the ask is only about 6 hours old. The request is marked completed (E022) and the workflow task was dismissed (E024), so this hold note is now the only follow-up prompt. Do not close the job while E023 is unanswered.
RECHECK Monday 22 September 2025:
1) If she has replied with costs and a responsibility view: log it. If she says any item is the former tenant's to pay, hand it to a person for the recharge/deposit decision; do not tell the tenant they will be charged.
2) If she has not replied: chase her by email and phone. Restate the E023 ask and also ask where the property keys are now (they were to be arranged through our office, E003). Give a reply-by date of Thu 25 Sept.
3) Close only when the E023 question is answered or she confirms she is making no claim, the key location is confirmed, and nothing is owed to Pineglass (stood down E020; their quote of £564.48 was declined, so no cost to us).
decision.rationale: This is a landlord-managed job. The landlord has confirmed completion herself, and for this kind of job her word is enough evidence of completion. No invoice comes to us because her own company did the work. The only open item is our own question to her (E023) about the cost breakdown and tenant responsibility, sent at 08:46 on 18 Sept, roughly 6 hours before the decision moment. Chasing within hours of an ask is premature, since landlords usually take hours to a few days to reply. We can't close yet either, because closing with an unanswered question is prohibited and nobody has confirmed where the keys to this vacant property are. The workflow task was dismissed (E024, E025), so the job could easily be forgotten. A hold note with a fixed recheck date guards against that. Thursday 18 Sept plus about 3 days lands on Monday 22 Sept, a working day. Sending her a second email now with extra asks (photos, invoice) would go beyond what a landlord-managed closure needs and would pile onto a request she has had for only a few hours. The key question can go into the Monday chase.
decision.expectedOutcome: The landlord replies to E023 by Monday 22 Sept, or she is chased with the key question added. The job stays open until the question and key location are settled.

Holding does not decide whether any cost is the former tenant's responsibility; any recharge needs a person and evidence such as the check-in inventory.
The 'completed' status in E022 does not mean the case can be closed.
No cost is approved or owed to Pineglass; their quote was declined.
